title: The day of burning
summary: The prophecy describes the coming day as a fire that consumes the proud and those who do wickedly.

explicit_facts.text: A coming day will burn like an oven.
The proud and those who do wickedly will be stubble, burned up with neither root nor branch remaining.

unspecified_visual_details: Any literal landscape, fire, or people shown; the verse gives a figurative prophecy, not a narrated visible event.

narration.text: the day cometh that shall burn as an oven
shall leave them neither root nor branch

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The burning and stubble imagery is figurative prophecy, not a literal scene to depict.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal supernatural fire event or identify visible people as the proud or wicked.

title: Healing and growth
summary: The prophecy promises healing and growth to those who fear the Lord's name.

explicit_facts.text: The Son of Righteousness will arise with healing for those who fear the Lord's name.
They will go forth and grow up as calves in a stall.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visible appearance of the Son of Righteousness, people, animals, or setting; the verse does not describe their appearance or narrate a present event.

narration.text: unto you that fear my name
shall the Son of Righteousness arise with healing in his wings
grow up as calves in the stall

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The image of calves in a stall is figurative teaching, not a narrated literal scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Son of Righteousness with an invented appearance or turn the metaphor into a literal event.

title: The wicked as ashes
summary: The prophecy says the wicked will be ashes under the feet of those addressed on the day the Lord acts.

explicit_facts.text: Those addressed will tread down the wicked, who will be ashes under their feet on the day the Lord acts.

unspecified_visual_details: Any literal people, ashes, feet, or location; the verse presents prophetic imagery rather than a narrated visible event.

narration.text: they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The ashes and treading imagery is figurative prophecy, not a literal scene to depict.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict people being burned, injured, or trampled.

title: Remember the law
summary: The Lord commands remembrance of the law of Moses, its statutes and judgments, given to Moses at Horeb for all Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commands the audience to remember the law of Moses, given to Moses at Horeb for all Israel, including its statutes and judgments.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether Moses or anyone else is visibly present, and the appearance of Horeb or any written law.

narration.text: Remember ye the law of Moses, my servant
which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moses and Horeb are referenced in narration; the verse does not place them physically in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Moses receiving the law as a present event.

title: Elijah foretold
summary: The Lord promises to send Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will send Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.

unspecified_visual_details: Elijah's appearance, setting, and any visible participants.

narration.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet
before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Elijah is mentioned in a promise about a future coming; the verse does not narrate his arrival.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Elijah appearing or performing an action in the present.

title: Hearts turned
summary: Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers and children toward one another, lest the Lord come and smite the earth with a curse.

explicit_facts.text: Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers.
This is so the Lord will not come and smite the earth with a curse.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether any fathers, children, or Elijah are visibly present, and their identities, appearances, or setting.

narration.text: he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children
and the heart of the children to their fathers

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The turning of hearts is figurative teaching; no specific family or present action is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a family, depict Elijah visibly, or portray the threatened curse as occurring.
